fired.detail: Alabama has no state wage-payment law setting a final-pay deadline; employers follow federal rules and their regular payday.
fired.cite: Ala. Dept. of Labor, Wage and Hour Info

quit.detail: No Alabama statute sets a deadline for employees who quit.
quit.cite: Ala. Dept. of Labor, Wage and Hour Info

accruedVacation.detail: With no state wage-and-hour law, vacation payout depends entirely on the employer's policy or contract.
accruedVacation.cite: Ala. Dept. of Labor, Wage and Hour Info

fired.detail: When the employer ends employment for any reason, final pay is due within three working days.

quit.value: Next regular payday at least 3 days after notice
quit.detail: When the employee quits, pay is due on the next regular payday that is at least three days after the employer receives notice.

accruedVacation.detail: An employer must pay out vacation only if it has a policy, promise or contract to do so.
accruedVacation.cite: Alaska Dept. of Labor, Wage and Hour FAQ

fired.value: Within 7 working days or end of next pay period, whichever is sooner
fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid within seven working days or by the end of the next regular pay period, whichever comes first.

quit.detail: An employee who quits must be paid by the regular payday for the pay period in which the termination occurred (by mail if requested).

fired.detail: An employer that discharges an employee must pay all wages due by the next regular payday; if not paid within 7 days after that payday, it owes double wages.
A discharged employee must be paid all wages, including accrued vacation, immediately at the time of termination.

quit.detail: An employee who quits without notice must be paid within 72 hours; one who gives at least 72 hours' notice must be paid on the last day.

accruedVacation.detail: Vested vacation is wages and cannot be forfeited at termination; 'use it or lose it' policies are illegal, though employers may cap accrual.
accruedVacation.cite: Cal. Lab. Code § 227.3; Suastez v. Plastic Dress-Up Co. (1982)

fired.detail: Wages are due immediately on discharge; if payroll is closed, within 6 hours of its next workday (24 hours if payroll is off-site).

quit.detail: When an employee quits or resigns, wages are due on the next regular payday.

accruedVacation.detail: If an employer provides paid vacation, it must pay all earned and determinable vacation pay at separation; vacation pay counts as wages.

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid in full no later than the business day after discharge.

quit.detail: An employee who quits must be paid in full by the next regular payday.

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued vacation must be paid only if an employer policy or collective bargaining agreement provides for payment at termination.

fired.value: Next regular payday or 3 business days, whichever is later
fired.detail: Final wages are due by the later of the next regular payday or three business days after the last day worked.

quit.value: Next regular payday or 3 business days, whichever is later
quit.detail: The same rule applies when an employee quits or resigns.

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid by the next working day (4 days if the employee handled the employer's money).

quit.value: Next regular payday or within 7 days, whichever is earlier
quit.detail: An employee who quits must be paid by the next regular payday or within 7 days, whichever comes first.

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid in full at the time of discharge, or by the next working day if immediate payment is impossible.

quit.value: Next regular payday (immediately with one pay period's notice)
quit.detail: An employee who quits is paid by the next regular payday, or at the time of quitting if at least one pay period's notice was given.

accruedVacation.detail: The Hawaii Supreme Court held that unused vacation is not 'wages' that must be paid at separation; payout depends on the employer's policy.
accruedVacation.cite: Casumpang v. ILWU Local 142, 108 Haw. 411 (2005) (annotated under HRS § 388-3)

fired.value: Next regular payday or within 10 days, whichever is earlier
fired.detail: Final wages are due by the earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days (excluding weekends and holidays); within 48 hours if the employee requests it in writing.

quit.value: Next regular payday or within 10 days, whichever is earlier
quit.detail: The same rule applies to resignations, including the 48-hour option on written request.

accruedVacation.detail: Idaho law does not require vacation pay; any payout depends on the employer's policy, contract or union agreement.
accruedVacation.cite: Idaho Dept. of Labor, Guide to Idaho Labor Laws

fired.detail: Final compensation must be paid at separation if possible, and no later than the next regularly scheduled payday.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who resign.

accruedVacation.detail: Earned vacation under a contract or policy must be paid out at the final rate of pay, and no policy may forfeit earned vacation at separation.

fired.detail: When an employer separates an employee from the payroll, unpaid wages are due on the regular payday for the pay period in which separation occurred.

quit.detail: Employees who leave voluntarily are also paid on the next regular payday (if the employer lacks their address, 10 business days after they provide one).

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued vacation is treated as compensation and an employee may be entitled to a pro-rata payout, but conditions in the employer's written policy or contract must be met.
accruedVacation.cite: Indiana state FAQ (vacation pay at separation)

fired.detail: Wages earned up to termination are due by the next regular payday for the period in which they were earned.

quit.detail: The same rule applies whether the employee quits or is terminated.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation must be paid only if due under an agreement or employer policy providing for accrued vacation.

fired.detail: Whether discharged or quitting, the employee must be paid by the next regular payday.

quit.detail: Whether discharged or quitting, the employee must be paid by the next regular payday.

accruedVacation.detail: Unused vacation is owed only if the employer has a policy or practice of paying it.
accruedVacation.cite: Kansas Dept. of Labor, Workplace Laws FAQ

fired.value: Next regular payday or 14 days, whichever is later
fired.detail: An employee who is discharged must be paid in full by the next normal pay period or 14 days after separation, whichever comes last.

quit.value: Next regular payday or 14 days, whichever is later
quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who leave voluntarily.

accruedVacation.detail: Vested vacation pay is defined as wages and must be paid with final wages; whether vacation vests depends on the employer's policy or agreement.

fired.value: Next regular payday or within 15 days, whichever is first
fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid by the next regular payday or within 15 days of discharge, whichever comes first.

quit.value: Next regular payday or within 15 days, whichever is first
quit.detail: An employee who resigns must be paid by the next regular payday for that pay cycle or within 15 days, whichever comes first.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation the employee has earned and is eligible to take under the employer's policy must be paid at separation, and earned vacation cannot be forfeited.

fired.detail: An employee leaving employment must be paid in full no later than the next established payday.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to any employee leaving employment.

accruedVacation.detail: Unused paid vacation accrued since Jan. 1, 2023 must be paid at separation, except for employers with 10 or fewer employees, public employers, or where a union contract says otherwise.

fired.detail: All wages due must be paid on or before the day they would have been paid if employment had continued.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to any termination of employment.

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued leave must be paid unless the employer has a written policy limiting payout, told the employee about it at hiring, and the policy denies payment.

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid in full on the day of discharge.

quit.detail: An employee who leaves must be paid in full on the next regular payday (or the following Saturday if there is no regular payday).

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation payments due under an oral or written agreement count as wages, so earned vacation must be paid with final wages.

fired.value: As soon as the amount can be determined
fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid all earned wages immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.

quit.value: As soon as the amount can be determined
quit.detail: An employee who quits must be paid all earned wages as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined.

accruedVacation.detail: Fringe benefits such as vacation are paid at termination only as required by the employer's written contract or written policy.
accruedVacation.cite: Mich. Comp. Laws § 408.473; Michigan LEO guidance

fired.detail: Earned wages are immediately due on discharge upon the employee's demand; the employer is in default if not paid within 24 hours of the demand.

quit.detail: Pay is due on the first regular payday after the last day; if that is less than 5 days away, by the second payday, but never more than 20 calendar days.

accruedVacation.detail: Minnesota wage law does not directly require payout; the employer's leave policy, contract or union agreement controls.
accruedVacation.cite: Minn. Dept. of Labor & Industry guidance

fired.detail: Unpaid wages are due on the day of discharge; if the employee requests payment in writing and it is not received within 7 days, penalty wages accrue.

quit.detail: Missouri law does not set a deadline for paying final wages to an employee who quits.

accruedVacation.detail: Employers need not provide or pay out vacation unless a contract establishes the benefit.

fired.value: Immediately (or next payday/15 days under written policy)
fired.detail: An employee separated for cause or laid off must be paid immediately unless a written policy extends payment to the next payday or 15 days, whichever is first.

quit.value: Next regular payday or 15 days, whichever is first
quit.detail: Final wages are due on the next regular payday for that pay period or within 15 days of separation, whichever comes first.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation is not mandatory, but once earned under the employer's policy it is wages due at separation; 'use it or lose it' policies are not allowed (caps are).
accruedVacation.cite: Mont. Dept. of Labor & Industry FAQ; Mont. Att'y Gen. Op. 23-56

fired.value: Next regular payday or within 2 weeks, whichever is sooner
fired.detail: When a private employer separates an employee, unpaid wages are due on the next regular payday or within two weeks, whichever is sooner.

quit.value: Next regular payday or within 2 weeks, whichever is sooner
quit.detail: The same rule applies to any separation from the payroll.

accruedVacation.detail: Earned but unused vacation leave is part of the wages due at separation.

fired.detail: Wages earned and unpaid at discharge are due and payable immediately.

quit.value: Next regular payday or 7 days, whichever is earlier
quit.detail: An employee who quits must be paid by the regular payday or within seven days, whichever comes first.

accruedVacation.detail: Nevada has no requirement to pay out unused vacation or paid leave unless the employer's policy or agreement provides for it.
accruedVacation.cite: Nev. Rev. Stat. § 608.0197; Nevada Labor Commissioner guidance

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid in full within 72 hours.

quit.value: Next regular payday (72 hours with one pay period's notice)
quit.detail: An employee who quits is paid by the next regular payday, or within 72 hours if at least one pay period's notice was given.

accruedVacation.detail: Paid vacation is not required; vacation pay counts as wages only when it is a matter of employer policy or practice, and the employer's policy controls payout.

fired.detail: When employment ends for any reason, all wages are due by the regular payday for the pay period in which the termination occurred.

quit.detail: The same rule applies when an employee quits.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation pay is not required by New Jersey law; if offered, it must be administered uniformly under the employer's policy or agreement.
accruedVacation.cite: N.J. Dept. of Labor, Wage and Hour FAQs

fired.value: Within 5 days (10 days for commission/task pay)
fired.detail: Fixed wages of a discharged employee are due within 5 days of discharge; wages based on tasks, pieces or commissions within 10 days.

quit.detail: An employee without a fixed-term contract who quits is paid on the next succeeding payday.

accruedVacation.detail: State law does not require vacation pay, but accrued, unused vacation owed under a written company policy is part of the final wages.
accruedVacation.cite: N.M. Dept. of Workforce Solutions, Wage and Hour FAQs

fired.detail: Wages are due by the regular payday for the pay period in which employment ended (by mail if requested).

quit.detail: The same rule applies however employment ends.

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued vacation must be paid at termination unless the employer's written policy explicitly provides for forfeiture.
accruedVacation.cite: N.Y. Lab. Law § 198-c; Industrial Board of Appeals decisions

fired.detail: Employees whose employment ends for any reason must be paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to any separation.

accruedVacation.detail: Employers need not offer vacation, but promised vacation must be paid per company policy; it can be forfeited only if employees were notified in writing of a forfeiture policy.

fired.detail: Unpaid wages are due on the regular paydays set in advance; for discharged employees, payment goes by certified mail unless otherwise agreed.

quit.detail: The same rule applies when an employee leaves voluntarily.

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued paid time off must be paid, except an employer may withhold it from an employee who quits with under 5 days' notice in the first year of employment if this was disclosed in writing at hiring.

fired.detail: Ohio has no separate final-pay deadline; wages follow the semimonthly schedule (first-half wages by the 1st of the next month, second-half by the 15th).

quit.detail: The same semimonthly schedule applies to employees who quit.

accruedVacation.detail: Ohio has no payout statute; courts enforce a clear handbook policy that forfeits unused vacation, but without such a policy accrued vacation can be recovered.
accruedVacation.cite: Broadstock v. Elmwood at the Springs, 2013-Ohio-969 (Ohio Ct. App.)

fired.detail: Whether an employee quits or is fired, the final paycheck is due on the next scheduled payday.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation payout counts as wages only if a written employer policy (such as a handbook) promises it.

fired.value: End of the next business day
fired.detail: When an employer discharges an employee (or by mutual agreement), all wages are due by the end of the first business day after termination.

quit.value: Immediately with 48 hours' notice; otherwise within 5 business days or next payday
quit.detail: With at least 48 hours' notice (excluding weekends and holidays), wages are due immediately; without it, within 5 business days or on the next regular payday, whichever is first.

accruedVacation.detail: There is no legal requirement to pay out accrued vacation, but employers must honor an established policy or agreement to do so.

fired.detail: When an employer separates an employee, wages are due no later than the next regular payday (by certified mail if requested).

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit or resign.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation pay is owed only if the employer has a policy or contract to pay it.
accruedVacation.cite: Pa. Dept. of Labor & Industry, Wage FAQs

fired.detail: Unpaid wages are due on the next regular payday (within 24 hours if the business is liquidating, merging, or moving out of state).

quit.detail: The same rule applies whether the employee separates or is separated.

accruedVacation.detail: After at least one year of service, vacation accrued under a policy or agreement becomes wages payable with final wages on the next regular payday.

fired.value: Within 48 hours or next regular payday (max 30 days)
fired.detail: When an employee is separated for any reason, wages are due within 48 hours or by the next regular payday, which may not be more than 30 days later.

quit.value: Within 48 hours or next regular payday (max 30 days)
quit.detail: The same rule applies to any separation.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation pay is owed as wages only when it is due under the employer's policy or an employment contract.

fired.detail: Wages are due by the next regular payday, or as soon after as the employee returns the employer's property.

quit.detail: An employee who quits is paid by the next regular payday, or once employer property is returned.

accruedVacation.detail: South Dakota has no law requiring paid leave; payout is a matter of employer policy or agreement.

fired.value: Next regular payday or 21 days, whichever is later
fired.detail: Final wages are due by the next regular payday after separation or 21 days after, whichever occurs last.

quit.value: Next regular payday or 21 days, whichever is later
quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit.

accruedVacation.detail: Unused vacation or PTO must be paid only if the employer's policy or labor agreement specifically requires it.

fired.detail: An employee who is laid off, fired or otherwise involuntarily separated must be paid within six calendar days of discharge.

quit.detail: An employee who quits or retires is paid on the next regularly scheduled payday after the resignation takes effect.

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued leave must be paid out only if a written policy or agreement promises it.

fired.detail: When an employer separates an employee, wages are due immediately and must be paid within 24 hours.

quit.detail: An employee without a fixed-term contract who resigns is paid on the next regular payday.

accruedVacation.detail: Accrued time off is owed at separation only if there is an agreement or policy to pay it.
accruedVacation.cite: Utah Labor Commission wage claim guidance

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid within 72 hours of discharge.

quit.detail: An employee who leaves voluntarily is paid on the next regular payday, or the following Friday if there is no regular payday.

accruedVacation.detail: Employers need not provide or pay out vacation, but are liable for vacation promised in a written agreement or handbook.
accruedVacation.cite: Vt. Dept. of Labor, Summary of Vermont Wage and Hour Laws

fired.detail: All wages due must be paid on or before the date they would have been paid had employment continued.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to any termination.

fired.detail: When employment ends by discharge or voluntary withdrawal, wages are due at the end of the established pay period.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit.

accruedVacation.detail: Washington does not require paid vacation or its payout; any payout depends on employer policy or a union contract.

fired.detail: Discharged employees must be paid on or before the next regular payday on which the wages would otherwise be due.

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit or resign.

accruedVacation.detail: The law does not require fringe benefits, but vacation earned and payable at separation under a written company policy is part of final wages.
accruedVacation.cite: W. Va. Code § 21-5-1(l); WV Division of Labor fact sheet

fired.detail: A discharged employee must be paid in full by the next regular payday (or within 31 days if earlier under the general pay rule).

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit.

accruedVacation.detail: Vacation is not required, but if a written vacation policy has no written forfeiture provision, earned unused vacation generally must be paid.
accruedVacation.cite: Wis. Dept. of Workforce Development guidance

fired.detail: Final wages are due no later than the employer's regularly scheduled payroll date (or as set by a union contract).

quit.detail: The same rule applies to employees who quit.

accruedVacation.detail: Earned vacation must be paid unless a clear written policy, acknowledged by the employee, denies payout; 'use it or lose it' is allowed only if there was a fair chance to use it.
accruedVacation.cite: Wyo. Stat. § 27-4-507; Wyoming DWS Labor Standards FAQ
